subject: Quantiles from Poisson Model Giving Curve

messages.author: 5f3476cb2c3d4aba
messages.subject: Quantiles from Poisson Model Giving Curve
parts:
I've been continuing with the log-Gaussian Cox models and feeling confident with what I'm getting from them now but I've got an issue that I can't seem to resolve. A probability plot of the quantiles results in a curve (as in the attached plot) rather than, as one would hope, something close to linear. Is there a reason that I may not have considered as to why this is happening?

The code is fairly simple where I'm considering the E and covariance matrix known so the call is just:
formula <- X ~ -1 + f(idx, model="matern2d", nu=1, nrow=n, ncol=n, constr=TRUE,
                      hyper=list(theta1=list(initial=log(1/v), fixed=TRUE),
                                 theta2=list(initial=log(p), fixed=TRUE)))
iTime <- system.time(inlaResult <- inla(formula, data=data.frame(X, idx),
                                        family="poisson", E=E, quantiles = q,
                                        control.inla=list(strategy="simplified.laplace"))) 

But this gives the following probability plot:

Any thoughts as to why this may be? What might I be overlooking?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Quantiles from Poisson Model Giving Curve
parts:
What quantiles are you comparing? The posterior quantiles of the log-linear predictor should not match quantiles of the data, so presumably you’re looking at something else.

Finn
